title: Unified Screening for Multiple Diseases
summary: Core empirical/theory linkage has demonstrated nonadditive cost and dependence mismatches. The literal independent-survival aggregation is not generally the target expectation, while historical evaluator/configuration remain unavailable. Conditional model results and positive comparative advantage are not globally refuted.
limitations: No author source execution, installation, clinical data access or empirical reproduction.
Historical raw arrays/configuration/final independent-survival evaluator unavailable.
Separate supplement availability unknown after OpenReview metadata403.
Conditional mathematical claims not universally refuted; all continuum regularity not certified.
No comprehensive errata search or external clinical literature audit.

problems.title: Nonadditive simulator costs differ from the costs used by the core characterization

source_claim.location: Eq1p5; AppendixB1p19; LemmaB7p20; Proposition4.1 proof pp22-23; Section5.1p8
source_claim.paraphrase: Disease-specific stopping produces additive costs and gap equality, then simulations validate the same structural model.

assumptions: Formal costs stop at own disease event/diagnosis or horizon
Pinned code stops on global unprevented event
One path with horizon40, disease1 no event/diagnosis, disease2 event20.5 and diagnosis1
Unit annual costs and source floor convention
problems.check: Pinned formulas give C10=20,C01=1,C11=41, hence C11-C01=40 != C10. Formal own-disease C10=40 regardless of second action. Subtracting fixed first-sample costs does not restore additivity.
problems.result: Simulator coefficients need not satisfy cost-gap identity used to prove the core decision rule/boundaries.
counterevidence: Global stopping can be an intended alternative model.
A general LP still works on nonadditive costs.
No entire-theorem or numerical-score collapse demonstrated.
problems.core_dependency: Additive cost gaps underpin core boundary characterization and asserted simulation agreement; common-budget comparator also depends on consistent accounting.
problems.impact: Major core theory-to-simulation mismatch. Need a common cost model before interpreting budget comparison.

correction.statement: Choose own-disease or global stopping consistently; rederive affected identities for global stopping; reevaluate budgets under one convention. No repaired execution.

problems.title: Observation laws violate claimed temporal or cross-disease conditional independence

source_claim.paraphrase: Conditional independence supports likelihood products and disease-wise survival factorization; shared random patient signal with independent errors is claimed to preserve independence.

assumptions: Text model S uniform01 fixed across visits, Gaussian errors sd.5
Pinned code instead uses binary mean and one (1,40) error row broadcast to two diseases
One-observation diagnostic equalrisks.5, both disease states1, threshold.95
problems.check: Text temporal covariance1/12,correlation.25. Pinned errors across diseases have covariance.25 and correlation1. Equal-disease one-step detection probability p=.318385; shared-noise joint p vs independence p^2=.101369.
problems.result: Text temporal claim is false; pinned generator separately changes cross-disease joint distribution needed by factorized survival analysis.
counterevidence: Pinned fixed-mean code is temporally independent; shared-signal temporal critique does not describe that code.
Dependence can be a legitimate alternate model requiring revised likelihood/joint analysis.
Common random numbers across actions are different from coupling diseases inside one simulated world.
problems.core_dependency: Posterior interpretation, joint survival coefficients and transfer of theoretical structure to empirical model.
problems.impact: Major mismatch in core empirical validation; not a refutation of factorization under actual conditional independence.

correction.statement: Specify latent-signal law and error dependence; separate disease noise rows for independent model or integrate joint dependent law. No author-code rerun.

problems.title: Independent comparator estimand and historical configuration require evidence

source_claim.paraphrase: Compare expected first-event survival at matched total budgets using independent referral policies and repeated simulations.

assumptions: Literal minimum of separate expectations is distinguished from per-trajectory minimum
Current pinned scripts need not match figure-generating historical revision
No raw policy or output arrays supplied
problems.check: Independent U,V each10or40 have E[min]=17.5, min(E)=25. Release has one policy variable per2Driskpoint with no nuisance-axis equality, unifiedbudget5 vsindependent5each, and argmaxrounding that can violate finiteLPbudget in general. Event-time and iteration configs differ from text.
problems.result: Actual reported .23 gain cannot be reconstructed from available evidence. Literal aggregation inflates independent comparator, so that isolated correction cannot erase a positive unified advantage.
counterevidence: D3 could mean correct per-trajectory minimum despite displayed expectation notation.
Population coefficients could hide missing equality constraints.
Pinned unifiedbudget5 is a disadvantage, not proof of favorable bias.
No observed rounding violation or ranking reversal measured.
problems.core_dependency: Main comparative empirical claim and stated independent-policy comparator.
problems.impact: Needs Evidence for historical scores, feasibility and estimand; exact displayed arithmetic correct.

correction.statement: Identify producing revision/config and joint reward evaluator; tie independent variables by ownrisk; report final costs afterrounding and fresh-trajectory uncertainty.
